Any data, record, image or sound that is generated, stored, received or sent in electronic form, such as emails, chats, CCTV footage or server logs.
A person or platform that receives, stores or transmits electronic records on behalf of others, such as telecom companies, ISPs, social media platforms, search engines and marketplaces.
Protection from liability that an intermediary gets for third-party content it hosts, provided it follows due diligence and acts on lawful takedown orders or court directions.
A person or organisation that, alone or with others, decides the purpose and means of processing personal data, for example a bank, hospital, app or employer.
The individual to whom the personal data relates; for a child or a person with a disability, this includes the parent or lawful guardian.
A person registered with the Data Protection Board who acts as a single point of contact to help data principals give, manage, review and withdraw consent through an accessible platform.

s: General term (also required in the BSA 2023 Schedule certificate under s.63(4)(c))
x: A fixed-length digital fingerprint (for example SHA-256) calculated from a file or disk; if even one bit changes, the hash changes, which helps prove evidence was not altered.
A documented record of who collected, handled, transferred and stored a piece of evidence, and when, so that its integrity can be shown in court.

s: BSA 2023 s.63 (old Indian Evidence Act 1872 s.65B)
x: A certificate that must accompany electronic evidence to make it admissible, identifying the record, the device and how it was produced; it was required under Section 65B of the old Evidence Act and now under BSA Section 63 with a Schedule format that includes hash values.
The Indian Computer Emergency Response Team, the national agency for responding to cyber security incidents, issuing alerts and giving directions on incident reporting and security practices.

s: IT Act 2000 s.69A; IT (Procedure and Safeguards for Blocking for Access of Information by Public) Rules 2009
x: A direction by the Central Government to an intermediary or government agency to block public access to specific online content on grounds such as sovereignty, security of the State or public order, following a prescribed procedure.
An officer appointed under the IT Act to decide claims for compensation and penalties for contraventions such as unauthorised access under Section 43, within the monetary limits set in the Act.

s: BNSS 2023 s.2(1)(g) (old CrPC s.2(c)); IT Act 2000 s.77B
x: An offence for which police can arrest without a warrant and start investigating without a Magistrate's order; under the IT Act, offences carrying three years' imprisonment and above are cognizable. Offences of exactly three years are also bailable; for offences above three years s.77B is silent on

s: BNSS 2023 s.359 (old CrPC s.320); IT Act 2000 s.77A
x: An offence that can be settled between the parties, with or without the court's permission, leading to acquittal; the IT Act allows courts to compound certain offences with exceptions. IT Act s.77A(2) still refers to old CrPC plea-bargaining sections; reading them as BNSS ss.289-300 is an interpreta

s: General term (offences may fall under IT Act 2000 s.66C, s.66D)
x: A fraud technique where messages, emails, calls or fake websites pretend to be a trusted source to trick people into revealing passwords, OTPs or financial details.
Faking the identity of a sender, such as a caller ID, email address, website or IP address, so that a message appears to come from someone trusted.

s: General term (offences may fall under IT Act 2000 s.66C, s.66D)
x: A fraud where a criminal gets a duplicate SIM for the victim's mobile number, often using fake documents or social engineering, to receive OTPs and take over bank or other accounts.
Authentication of an electronic record using an asymmetric cryptosystem and hash function, backed by a Digital Signature Certificate issued by a licensed Certifying Authority.
A broader, technology-neutral term for authenticating an electronic record by reliable techniques listed in the Second Schedule, including digital signatures and Aadhaar-based eSign.
An entity licensed by the Controller of Certifying Authorities to issue electronic signature or Digital Signature Certificates.

A data fiduciary notified by the Central Government based on factors like volume and sensitivity of data and risk to rights, which must meet extra obligations such as appointing a Data Protection Officer and running audits and impact assessments.

The body set up under the DPDP Act to inquire into personal data breaches and complaints against data fiduciaries and consent managers, and to impose penalties. The Board was set up from 13 November 2025, but its complaint and penalty powers apply only from around 13 May 2027 (being verified).

Any unauthorised processing, accidental disclosure, acquisition, sharing, alteration, destruction or loss of access to personal data that compromises its confidentiality, integrity or availability; data fiduciaries must intimate such breaches to the Board and affected persons once that duty starts,

s: IT Act 2000 s.43A; SPDI Rules 2011 r.8; DPDP Act 2023 s.44(2)(a)
x: Security practices and procedures a body corporate handling sensitive personal data must implement, such as a documented information security programme; the IT Act compensation provision on this stays in force until DPDP Act s.44(2) omits it, around 13 May 2027 (being verified).

Under the 2011 IT Rules, personal information such as passwords, financial details, health and medical records, sexual orientation and biometric information. These rules still apply until DPDP Act s.44(2) commences (around 13 May 2027).

s: IT Rules 2021 r.3(2); SPDI Rules 2011 r.5(9)
x: An officer whom intermediaries and body corporates must designate and publish contact details for, to receive and resolve user complaints within the timelines set in the rules: for intermediaries, acknowledgement within 24 hours and resolution within 7 days under the 2026 amendment (being verified).

s: IT Act 2000 s.79(2)(c); IT Rules 2021 r.3(1)
x: The obligations intermediaries must follow to keep safe harbour, such as publishing rules and privacy policies, acting on court or government orders and informing users not to share unlawful content.
A bit-by-bit copy of a storage device, including deleted and unallocated space, made so analysis can be done on the copy while the original stays untouched; its hash is recorded to prove it matches.
A hardware or software tool that lets investigators read a storage device without writing any data to it, preserving the original evidence.
Data about data, such as a file's creation date, author, device model, GPS location in a photo or email header details, often crucial in establishing timelines.

s: IT Act 2000 s.67C; CERT-In Directions dated 28.04.2022 under IT Act s.70B(6)
x: An IP address identifies a device or connection on a network, and logs record activity linked to it; intermediaries must preserve certain information, and CERT-In directions require covered entities to maintain logs of all ICT systems for a rolling 180 days, within India.

s: General term (offences may fall under BNS 2023 s.204, s.308, s.318, s.319; IT Act 2000 s.66D)
x: A scam, not a legal procedure, in which fraudsters pose as police, CBI, customs or other officials on video calls, falsely claim the victim is under 'arrest' and pressure them to transfer money.

s: IT Rules Amendment 2026, G.S.R. 120(E), r.2(1)(wa) and r.3(3)
x: Audio, video or images created or altered with AI to realistically show a person saying or doing something they did not; the IT Rules now regulate this as 'synthetically generated information'.
Fraudulently or dishonestly using another person's electronic signature, password or other unique identification feature.

s: IT Act 2000 s.66D; BNS 2023 s.319 (old IPC s.416, s.419)
x: Cheating someone by pretending to be another person, including by using a computer resource or communication device, such as fake customer care or fake profiles.

s: General term (offences may fall under IT Act 2000 s.66E, s.67, s.67A; BNS 2023 s.308, s.351)
x: Threatening to publish intimate or morphed images or videos of a person unless they pay money or provide more content or favours.

s: IT Act 2000 s.43 Explanation (computer contaminant, computer virus); s.43; s.66
x: Malware is any software designed to damage systems, steal data or gain unauthorised access, and ransomware is malware that encrypts or locks data and demands payment to restore it; the IT Act uses the terms 'computer contaminant' and 'computer virus'.

A Zero FIR can be lodged at any police station regardless of where the offence happened, and information can be given by electronic communication, which is taken on record once signed by the informant within three days.

s: IT Act 2000 s.48 (as amended by Finance Act 2017 s.169); DPDP Act 2023 s.29; DPDP Act 2023 s.44(1)
x: Appeals against IT Act adjudicating officer orders originally went to the Cyber Appellate Tribunal, which was merged into the Telecom Disputes Settlement and Appellate Tribunal (TDSAT) by the Finance Act 2017; TDSAT is also the appellate tribunal under the DPDP Act.

s: General term (MHA initiative, no specific statute)
x: The Indian Cyber Crime Coordination Centre is a Ministry of Home Affairs initiative that coordinates action against cybercrime and runs the National Cyber Crime Reporting Portal (cybercrime.gov.in) and the 1930 helpline for reporting financial cyber fraud.

Shows open sockets: listening ports, established connections and the process that owns each one. Modern replacement for netstat. sudo ss -tulpn
Legacy tool from net-tools that lists connections, listening ports, routing tables and interface statistics. sudo netstat -tulpn
Shows the IP addresses and state of every network interface (use ip link or ip addr without -br to see MAC addresses). ip -br addr show
Displays the kernel routing table, including the default gateway. ip route show
Captures and prints network packets on an interface, with powerful filters. Can also save captures to a pcap file for Wireshark. sudo tcpdump -i eth0 -nn -c 50 port 53
Queries the systemd journal, the central log store on most modern Linux systems. journalctl -u ssh.service --since today
Controls and inspects systemd services, timers and other units. systemctl list-units --type=service --state=running
Lists running processes with their PID, parent, owner and full command line. ps -ef --forest
Lists open files, and because sockets are files, shows which process holds which network connection. sudo lsof -i -P -n
Searches the filesystem by name, type, owner, size, permissions or modification time. sudo find /etc /usr/local/bin -type f -mtime -2 -ls
Changes file permission bits (read, write, execute) for owner, group and others. chmod 600 ~/.ssh/id_ed25519
Changes the owner and group of files and directories. sudo chown root:root /etc/cron.d/backup
Lists all files including hidden dot files, with permissions, owner, size and date. ls -la /tmp
Shows detailed metadata for a file: size, permissions, owner, inode and access, modify and change times. stat /etc/passwd
Computes or verifies SHA256 hashes of files. sha256sum ubuntu.iso
Searches text or files for lines that match a pattern or regular expression. grep -i "failed password" /var/log/auth.log
Shows the history of user logins, logouts and reboots from the wtmp file. last -F -n 20
Shows who is logged in right now, with terminal and login time. who -a
Prints the user ID, group ID and all groups of a user. id alice
Lists the commands a user is allowed to run with sudo, as defined in sudoers. sudo -l -U alice
Lists the scheduled cron jobs of the current user, or of another user when run as root. sudo crontab -l -u alice
Lists the rules in the netfilter firewall tables with packet and byte counters. sudo iptables -L -n -v --line-numbers
Shows the path packets take to a destination, hop by hop, with round trip times. traceroute -n example.com
PowerShell cmdlet that reads Windows event logs and ETW logs with fast filtering. Get-WinEvent -FilterHashtable @{LogName='Security'; Id=4625} -MaxEvents 20
Lists TCP connections and listening ports with the owning process ID. Get-NetTCPConnection -State Listen | Select-Object LocalAddress,LocalPort,OwningProcess
Lists running processes with CPU, memory, ID and optional file path. Get-Process | Sort-Object CPU -Descending | Select-Object -First 10 Name,Id,CPU,Path
Lists Windows services and their status. Get-Service | Where-Object Status -eq 'Running'
Lists local user accounts on the machine. Get-LocalUser | Select-Object Name,Enabled,LastLogon
Lists the members of a local group. Get-LocalGroupMember -Group "Administrators"
Computes the hash of a file, SHA256 by default. Get-FileHash .\setup.exe -Algorithm SHA256
Lists scheduled tasks with their path and state. Get-ScheduledTask | Where-Object State -ne 'Disabled' | Select-Object TaskPath,TaskName,State
Shows the status of Microsoft Defender Antivirus on the machine. Get-MpComputerStatus | Select-Object AMServiceEnabled,RealTimeProtectionEnabled,AntivirusSignatureLastUpdated
Command line tool to query, export and manage Windows event logs. wevtutil qe Security /c:5 /rd:true /f:text
Shows all connections and listening ports with numeric addresses and the owning process ID. netstat -ano
Shows full IP configuration for every adapter: IP, MAC, gateway, DNS servers and DHCP details. ipconfig /all
Shows the security privileges held by the current user token. whoami /priv
Lists running processes in cmd, with optional service and module details. tasklist /svc
Lists scheduled tasks from cmd, with full details in verbose mode. schtasks /query /fo LIST /v
Lists local user accounts, or shows details for one account. net user alice
Displays or changes NTFS access control lists on files and folders. icacls C:\Shares\Finance
Tests connectivity to a host, including whether a specific TCP port is reachable. Test-NetConnection -ComputerName server01 -Port 443
PowerShell DNS lookup tool that queries any record type. Resolve-DnsName example.com -Type MX
Windows traceroute: shows each router hop to a destination with timings. tracert -d example.com
Shows which Windows audit policy categories are logged (success, failure or none). auditpol /get /category:*
Open source network scanner that discovers hosts, open ports and service versions. nmap -sn 192.168.1.0/24

Fetches only the HTTP response headers of a URL. curl -I https://example.com
Shows the ARP cache: IP to MAC address mappings the host has learned on the local network. arp -a
Displays the configuration currently active in RAM on the router or switch. show running-config | section line vty
One line summary of every interface: IP address, status and protocol state. show ip interface brief
Detailed status and counters for interfaces: errors, drops, speed, duplex and traffic rates. show interfaces GigabitEthernet0/1
Lists VLANs on a switch with their names, status and access ports. show vlan brief

Lists directly connected Cisco devices discovered with Cisco Discovery Protocol. show cdp neighbors detail
Displays configured access control lists with per rule match counters. show access-lists
Shows syslog settings and the contents of the local logging buffer. show logging | include SEC_LOGIN
Displays the IPv4 routing table with how each route was learned. show ip route
Shows the IOS version, uptime, hardware model, serial number and last reload reason. show version
